data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"An idempotent operation is one whose repeated application yields the same result as a single application (f\u2218f = f), whereas a safe operation is one whose repetition produces no harmful side effects even if the resulting state differs from a single execution. An append-only event log requires safety\u2014not strict idempotency\u2014from its writers: at-least-once delivery may produce duplicate entries, but append-only semantics guarantee that retries never corrupt or overwrite prior entries, and downstream consumers can deduplicate. Idempotency becomes achievable if the log uses content-addressable storage (hash of event content as the key), collapsing the distinction for that specific construction.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If consumers cannot deduplicate events (e.g., no globally unique event IDs are available), then safety alone is insufficient and strict idempotency becomes required.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If duplicate appends cause unbounded log growth that exhausts storage before deduplication can occur, the operation is neither safe nor idempotent under at-least-once delivery.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the append operation has external side effects beyond writing to the log (e.g., triggering downstream notifications per append), safety may fail even though the log itself remains append-only.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Idempotency is an algebraic property of a function: f(f(x)) = f(x) for all inputs. Safety is a weaker, system-level property: repeated execution does not violate system invariants or cause incorrect observable behavior, even if the resulting state differs from a single execution. In an append-only log under at-least-once delivery, a retried append that writes a duplicate event is safe (prior entries are immutable; the log remains a valid history) but not strictly idempotent (the log now contains a duplicate, so the observable state differs). The system survives by treating duplicates as a transport-level artifact rather than a correctness violation, making safety the necessary and sufficient condition. Content-addressable storage transforms append into a map insertion keyed by content hash, which is idempotent by construction\u2014but this is an implementation choice, not a requirement of append-only logs in general.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
